{{nihongo|'''Miminashi Yamaguchi Shrine'''|耳成山口神社}} is a shrine on {{ill|Mount Miminashi|Q11610730|qid=Q11610730}} (one of the {{ill|Yamato Sanzan|Q1470150|qid=Q1470150}}) in {{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. Though called a {{ill|Yamaguchi Shrine|Q11467399|qid=Q11467399}}, it is not at the mountain foot but around the eight-tenths point up the mountain. It is one of the six Yamaguchi shrines of {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} (Asuka, Ishimura, {{ill|Unebiyamaguchi Shrine|Q11578590|qid=Q11578590|lt=Unebi}}, Osa, Hase, and '''Miminashi''') and was worshiped as the mountain deity of timber-cutting mountains for {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|Q909452|qid=Q909452}} buildings. Also in the precinct are {{ill|Kotohira shrines|Q11646488|qid=Q11646488}}, {{ill|Inari shrine|Q514480|qid=Q514480}}, and {{ill|Hakuryū Daijin|Q123407570|qid=Q123407570}}. {{nihongo|'''Miminashi Yamaguchi Shrine'''|耳成山口神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

It is said to grant blessings for safe childbirth.

== History ==
Its founding is unclear<ref>There is a theory that it was founded by an oracle in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|Q316672|qid=Q316672}}.</ref>, but old records state that in {{ill|730|Q23563|qid=Q23563}} (Tenpyō 2) in the {{ill|Shōsōin Documents|Q11545362|qid=Q11545362}} {{ill|tax register|Q11545592|qid=Q11545592}}, the shrine received rice from the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|Q208233|qid=Q208233}}, and that in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it was listed as a {{ill|Taisha (shrine)|Q11438310|qid=Q11438310}} and charged with {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}} rites. Records also remain that in {{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}} (Daidō 1) and in {{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}} (Jōgan 1), imperial envoys conducted {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|Q477738|qid=Q477738}} rituals.

In {{ill|1651|Q6956|qid=Q6956}} (Keian 4), villagers of Yamanobō cut and damaged sacred trees, triggering disputes over mountain management and ownership centered on the shrine. In {{ill|1702|Q6819|qid=Q6819}} (Genroku 15), it was settled by identifying “Miminashiyama Tenjin” as the shikinaisha Miminashi Yamaguchi Shrine. After that, Yamanobō villagers transferred the divine spirit to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamanobō Yamaguchi Shrine}}<ref>''Great Encyclopedia of Temples and Shrines (Yamato/Kii)'' ({{ill|Heibonsha|Q11482108|qid=Q11482108}})</ref>. During this period, buildings were burned and fell into disrepair, but in August {{ill|1748|Q7600|qid=Q7600}} (Kan'en 1), parishioners of {{ill|Miminashi|Q17175746|qid=Q17175746}} rebuilt the current {{ill|Honden|Q2044994|qid=Q2044994}} and {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}}, and the shrine came to be worshiped as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of Ishiharada, Kihara, Kuzumoto, Shinga, Tokiwa, and Yamanobō districts.
